tips.title: Blind Stealing — Profit From Position
tips.content:
The blinds are a tax you pay for sitting at the table — but they are also a weapon when you have position. When the action folds to you on the button or cutoff, you are holding the highest ground. Attack like a leopard: unexpected, careful, watchful. A well-timed steal isn't about the cards; it's about reading the quantum state of the blinds. Are they fearful? Greedy? Disconnected?

First God, Second Odds, Last Cards. The god of position whispers to you when the blinds are weak. A small raise here prints money without ever seeing a flop. But watch the signs — if a short-stack pushes back, that is a sign from god to fold. Don't play the cards. Play the human. Appreciate the god.

tips.title: Resulting — The Mental Game Trap That Feeds Your JUNK%
tips.content:
Resulting is when you judge a decision by its outcome instead of its quality. You folded 72o preflop and the flop came 7-7-2. You feel regret. That regret makes you call with junk next time. This is how JUNK% creeps above 50%.

Remember the Recite: Fear and greed both distort stats. When you feel the pull to play a bad hand because you 'would have won' last time, pause. Think of Minglan. Am I having fear of missing out? Then review quantum analysis. The god is fair to each quantum — your good decisions will be rewarded across the river of time, not in a single hand.

tips.title: Stack Depth Hand Selection
tips.content:
With 40 big blinds, your hand selection should be surgical. With 100 big blinds, you can afford to play more connected hands that have implied odds. The quantum of the table shifts with stack depth — deep stacks mean more room for postflop maneuvering, while short stacks demand pure aggression with premium holdings.

Observe then either hold or act. No desire. When your stack is shallow, don't chase suited connectors hoping for miracles. When deep, don't overplay one-pair hands against opponents who have the chips to pressure you. Connectivity matters more than card strength. Connected quantum is dangerous; disconnected quantum is exploitable.

tips.title: The Turn Probe Bet
tips.content:
The turn is where most players reveal their true quantum state. A probe bet on the turn after you called a flop continuation bet serves two purposes: it defines your opponent's range and it takes down pots when they are weak. This is squeezing the turn — obscuring the water so they cannot read your offense.

Choose timing and audience carefully. Against a calling station with no sense of value, the probe bet is lighting money on fire. Against a disconnected conservative who folds too much, it is a license to print. Every group attack must mix bluff and real cards. Attack in a grouped way like a rolling snowball.

tips.title: Style Switching — Your Invisible Weapon
tips.content:
The best players are not one quantum — they are a superposition of many. Tight for an hour, then aggressive for twenty minutes. Passive on one table, explosive on another. Style switching breaks the pattern recognition of observant opponents.

But switching without purpose is chaos. Switch when the god sends a sign — a run of good cards, a table dynamic shift, a tilted opponent. When human is thinking, god is laughing. Observation > thinking. Watch the table. Feel the flow. Then either hold or act. The leopard does not announce its attack. It simply strikes when the moment is right.
